findings.description: The 'data' bucket sets no ACL/public access block and is explicitly commented as public, so bucket contents (including an uploaded customer master file) can be read by anonymous internet users. No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for it.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects containing customer data are stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorized access to this public bucket would leave no audit trail in S3 server access logs.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects overwritten or deleted (maliciously or accidentally) cannot be recovered, and the whole bucket can be destroyed with contents.
A file named 'customer-master.xlsx' — likely containing sensitive customer records — is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.data, which is public and unencrypted, exposing the data to anonymous readers.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is set for the financials bucket, leaving financial data stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is defined, so access to sensitive financial data is not auditable via S3 server access logs.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, so deletion or tampering of financial objects is unrecoverable.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the bucket, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could silently make the financial data public.
No server-side encryption configuration is defined for the operations bucket, so objects are stored without enforced encryption.
No logging block is configured, leaving no audit trail of object-level access to this bucket.
No public access block resource restricts this bucket, so future ACLs or policies could expose it publicly.
The data science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so its data (often derived from sensitive source datasets) is stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined, leaving the bucket without a defence-in-depth guard against accidental public exposure.
The central log bucket has no public access block; log data can reveal internal access patterns and identifiers if a policy or ACL later exposes it.
force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket allows all log objects to be deleted in a single terraform destroy, undermining forensic evidence retention.
None of the buckets, including the log bucket, enforce aws:SecureTransport via a bucket policy, so data may be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.
